title: Security review + threat model for SIEM audit-log exporter (secrets, egress/SSRF, leakage, encryption/logging)
creator: Marcus Lin
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
description:
Goal: complete Security Engineering threat model + sign-off for the SIEM-ready audit export beta (hosted + dedicated). Scope is exporter service + destination adapters (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, S3), control-plane config surface, secret handling, and operational surfaces.

This ticket is the gating security review for beta enablement (tenant allowlist). It should produce: (1) a concrete threat model write-up for audit export, (2) actionable mitigations tracked as follow-up issues/PRs, and (3) explicit sign-off criteria for Security + SRE.

Primary areas to review:
- Secrets handling: destination credentials (Splunk HEC token, Datadog API key, AWS role/KMS key IDs), storage, access controls, rotation, redaction in logs.
- SSRF / egress controls: prevent arbitrary outbound requests; destination validation; allowlist strategy; DNS / IP / redirect handling; private IP ranges.
- Data leakage: tenant isolation, cross-tenant config sync, queue separation, DLQ and replay tooling safety, metrics cardinality/labels, structured logs.
- Encryption: in transit to destinations, at rest for checkpoints/DLQ/state, KMS usage, and customer-provided keys where applicable.
- Logging: ensure exporter logs do not contain audit payloads/PII; ensure debug logs are safe; ensure audit event schema v2 meets redaction policy.

References:
- Confluence: Audit event schema v2 + SIEM mapping: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-event-schema-v2-and-siem-mapping.json
- Confluence: PII redaction policy: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/pii-redaction-and-sensitive-fields-policy-for-audit-events.json
- ADR: Delivery semantics + idempotency: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-audit-export-delivery-semantics-and-idempotency.json
- Exporter architecture: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/audit-exporter-service-architecture.json
- Slack thread (security review coordination): sources/slack/eng-security/1737395528.json
acceptance_criteria:
1) Threat model documented in this ticket (assets, trust boundaries, threats, mitigations).
2) Explicit list of required mitigations for beta, with owners and links to PRs/issues.
3) Secrets handling meets Security requirements: stored only in approved secret store, never logged, rotation path documented.
4) Egress/SSRF controls implemented: destination validation + allowlist hooks; no arbitrary host/port; safe DNS resolution; block private/reserved ranges.
5) Exporter logs/metrics reviewed for data leakage: no raw audit payloads; bounded cardinality; sensitive fields redacted.
6) Encryption posture confirmed: TLS to destinations; at-rest encryption for internal state; SSE-S3/SSE-KMS for S3 delivery supported.
7) Security sign-off recorded (Marcus Lin + Dr. Aisha Rahman delegate if needed) and SRE readiness acknowledged (Sean Gallagher).

threat_model:
System: Audit Exporter (at-least-once) delivering Redwood audit events to customer-controlled SIEM destinations: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, and S3.

In-scope components:
- Control plane export config APIs/UI (destinations, filters, secret references, backfill window)
- Exporter service (config sync, filtering, batching, checkpointing, retries, DLQ)
- Destination adapters (Splunk, Datadog, S3)
- Observability (metrics, logs, traces) and operator tooling (pause, replay)

Out of scope (beta): Private/on-prem deployment constraints; customer-managed egress proxies beyond documented patterns.

Data flow (high level):
1) Audit events are emitted by core services using audit schema v2 (includes event_id, timestamps, actor/action/resource, tenant/workspace, optional src_ip/user_agent where allowed).
2) Exporter consumes events via internal stream/queue scoped per region. Exporter fetches/export-config from control plane, scoped by tenant.
3) Exporter applies filters and batches events. State (checkpoints/DLQ pointers) persisted.
4) Adapter sends batch to destination over TLS (HEC/Datadog) or writes objects to S3 (SSE-S3/SSE-KMS options).

Assets:
- Audit event content (sensitive operational/security data)
- Destination credentials (HEC token, Datadog API key, AWS role + external ID + KMS key IDs)
- Export configuration (filters may reveal internal resource names)
- Exporter internal state (checkpoints, DLQ payloads)
- Observability data (logs/metrics/traces)

Trust boundaries:
- Redwood control plane ↔ exporter service (config sync)
- Exporter ↔ external customer endpoints (Splunk/Datadog) over public internet
- Exporter ↔ AWS S3 (customer bucket) often cross-account
- Operator access to pause/replay tooling

Primary threats and required mitigations (Beta MUST):
A) SSRF / data exfil via arbitrary destination URLs
- Threat: attacker (or compromised admin) configures destination to internal IP/metadata endpoints or attacker-controlled host, leading to exfil of audit stream.
- Mitigations:
  - Destination URL validation: only https; restricted ports; no redirects; explicit hostname parsing; reject userinfo in URL.
  - DNS/IP validation: resolve hostname and block private/reserved ranges (RFC1918, link-local, loopback, metadata ranges); re-check periodically to reduce DNS rebinding risk.
  - Egress allowlist hook: outbound requests must pass allowlist policy (initially: Datadog known domains, Splunk HEC customer domains optionally allowlisted per tenant; S3 via AWS endpoints).
  - Observability: emit metric/event when destination rejected by policy (no payload).
  - Implementation: PR-1105.

B) Secret leakage (logs, metrics, config surfaces)
- Threat: credentials appear in structured logs, traces, error messages, or are stored in plaintext.
- Mitigations:
  - Control plane stores secret references only (secret_id), not raw tokens/keys.
  - Exporter logs: redact Authorization headers and any field matching configured sensitive keys; enforce structured logging schema.
  - Prevent high-verbosity logging in production (debug gated, audited).
  - Rotation: document supported rotation path (create new secret, update destination to new secret ref, confirm health, revoke old). Ensure exporter handles changes without emitting secrets.

C) Cross-tenant leakage (config sync, queueing, DLQ/replay)
- Threat: exporter processes events from tenant A using tenant B config or writes to B’s destination.
- Mitigations:
  - Config sync must be tenant-scoped, authenticated, and validated; exporter caches config per-tenant with explicit tenant_id keys.
  - Queue consumption isolated by tenant partition key; add invariant checks: event.tenant_id must match config.tenant_id before send; fail closed.
  - DLQ and replay tooling must require explicit tenant + destination selection and include guardrails (rate-limit, max batch size, confirm prompts).

D) Data leakage via observability
- Threat: raw audit event data leaks into logs/metrics/traces or creates high-cardinality metrics that expose resource identifiers.
- Mitigations:
  - Logs: do not log raw event JSON. Allowed fields: event_id, category, action, tenant_id (hashed optional), destination_type, adapter status code, retry_count.
  - Metrics: labels bounded; no resource IDs, user emails, IPs. Prefer aggregation by destination_type + region + result.
  - Traces: disable payload capture; keep spans minimal.

E) Encryption gaps
- Threat: audit data exposed in transit or at rest.
- Mitigations:
  - In transit: TLS required for Splunk/Datadog; enforce https.
  - At rest: exporter state stores use platform-standard encryption at rest; S3 objects use SSE-S3 by default, optionally SSE-KMS (customer key) and cross-account role support.
  - Implementation: S3 SSE-KMS + assume-role documented/implemented in PR-1068.

F) Denial of service / backpressure and unsafe retries
- Threat: downstream rate limiting causes exporter retries leading to backlog, resource exhaustion, or operator-triggered replay storms.
- Mitigations:
  - Retry with exponential backoff + jitter; per-destination circuit breaker.
  - Auto-pause on sustained errors or max lag threshold; require operator action to resume.
  - DLQ and replay tooling includes throttles and safety checks.

Residual risk (accepted for Beta with constraints):
- Exact once delivery not provided (at-least-once). Customers must deduplicate using event_id.
- Customer-configured Splunk endpoints may require per-tenant allowlisting / review depending on domain pattern; beta cohort is small and manually approved.

Sign-off conditions:
- MUST mitigations implemented and verified in staging.
- Runbook updated for pause/resume/replay and credential rotation.
- Metrics/alerts in place for lag + error spikes; on-call paging policy reviewed.
